title: Kernel / User Mode Boundary
description: Interactive SVG stack diagram of the user-mode (ring 3) / kernel-mode (ring 0) boundary, showing applications, the system-call interface, kernel subsystems, and hardware. Hover any layer for an explanation of why the privilege boundary matters.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Operating system privilege rings and the system call boundary
learningObjectives: Explain why user-mode processes cannot touch hardware directly.
Identify the system call interface as the only legal path from ring 3 to ring 0.
Reason about why a kernel bug is a total compromise while a user-process bug is contained.
educational.prerequisites: Basic idea of an operating system and processes.

pedagogical.modelType: static layered diagram with hover reveals
controls: Hover/tap the system call interface line
pedagogical.assessment: Students trace a file read from a user application down through the syscall boundary to hardware and explain each privilege transition.
misconceptionsAddressed: Assuming a sandboxed user process can compromise the whole system without crossing the kernel boundary.
